facts.fact: Kenya News Agency reports that on 2026-07-29 Kenya and Tanzania ministers launched at the Lunga Lunga/Horohoro border a cross-border project joining Kenya's national broadband backbone and submarine cable infrastructure with Tanzania's, implemented by Kenya's ICT Authority and TTCL; it does not say the link is lit.

facts.fact: Africa50 partnered with Bayobab (MTN) in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a roughly US$320m terrestrial fibre network across ten or more African countries including Tanzania; the document gives no construction start.

note: Tanzania is named only in a startup-activity tier list; nothing on shared links or facilities.

facts.fact: Daily News reported that Tanzania and the DRC agreed to accelerate a fibre-optic cable from Kigoma in Tanzania to Kalemie in DRC across Lake Tanganyika, a commitment their foreign minister reaffirmed at a meeting in Dar es Salaam; the two are described as pursuing its construction, with no cost, contract, start of works or timetable stated and no date given for the original agreement.

facts.fact: AfriqueITNews reports that on 20 October 2025 the heads of Congo's SOCOF and Tanzania's TTCL, with a Tanzanian ministry representative, made official the Kalemie-Kigoma lake cable, with works due in Q1 2026 and service by end 2027.

TechAfrica News reports the Dar-es-Salaam to Mombasa terrestrial fibre link was officially launched on 21 July 2025 at the Lunga Lunga/Horohoro border, a joint effort of Kenya's ICT Authority and TTCL, connecting Kenya's NICTBB to Tanzania's national fibre network.
